correctness.rationale: Independently, place one edge at u=(0,0), v=(L,0) and put B=(b,h), h>0. A ray from B in direction w meets the lens up to the positive part of min((u−B)·w,(v−B)·w). On the right and left half-circles the respective controlling radial endpoints are a sin(alpha−phi) and q sin(beta−phi), positive for 0≤phi<alpha or beta, where a,q are the endpoint distances and alpha,beta the endpoint angles. Integrating half the squared radius gives (alpha a²+beta q²)/4−[a² sin(2alpha)+q² sin(2beta)]/8. The bracket is 2h[b+(L−b)]=2hL. This works even for an exterior perpendicular foot, when the frozen sector argument must not subtract both unsigned triangle areas. Summing over edges sums the fan triangle areas to A(P) and the split angles to the original interior angles. Completing the weighted square gives the unique interior minimizer, because all weights are positive and the vertices span P. Convex weights expressing B in a triangle show that any point in all three diameter disks equals B, so the pair sum gives double coverage in area. The formula and claims hold as stated.
residual_risks: Uploaded numerical checks not replayed. The proof covers obtuse fan triangles via the ray integral; the frozen sector prose needs signed segment corrections in that case. It does not give the area covered at least twice for polygons with m>3.
